intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk, surrounded by lush green valleys and gentle morning breezes. Many local instructors offer small group classes here, blending movement with Bali's natural beauty.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, then unwind and watch one of Bali's legendary sunsets. Instructors are widely available along the beach and equipment is included in most lesson packages.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Bali's world-renowned yoga culture with daily drop-in classes at The Yoga Barn, one of Asia's most celebrated wellness centers. Choose from Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, and meditation sessions across a lush jungle setting.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at the pristine white-sand beaches of Nusa Dua, known for calm turquoise waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Rent a sun lounger, explore the coral reefs, and enjoy fresh coconuts from beachside vendors.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Organic Market Visit
experiences.description: Start your morning at a traditional local market selecting fresh spices and tropical ingredients, then learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes like satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding under the guidance of a local chef.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali Airport at 13:00 — skip morning slot
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00. Take a pre-booked budget airport shuttle or shared Grab ride to Aegean Bliss Resort (~45–60 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Indian Ocean and watch the afternoon waves.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest beach strip on foot. Watch the Bali sunset from the shoreline — one of the island's most iconic free experiences. Browse local warungs (small family-run eateries) near the resort for a relaxed first dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable nasi goreng or mie goreng from a local warung near the airport or resort area (~IDR 25,000–40,000 / ~$1.50–$2.50)
meals.dinner: Warung dinner near the beach — try ayam bakar (grilled chicken) with rice and a fresh coconut water (~IDR 50,000–70,000 / ~$3–$4.50)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities start only after 13:00 arrival. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport for immediate needs but use ATMs in town for better rates. Avoid unlicensed taxis — use Grab or Blue Bird.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a free sunrise yoga session on the beach in front of the resort. Many Bali beaches have open-air yoga spots or you can simply practice on the sand. Follow with a refreshing swim in the calm morning sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or scooter (~IDR 50,000–80,000/day) and explore the surrounding coastal village. Visit a nearby local market to sample tropical fruits like salak, rambutan, and mangosteen. Head to a quieter neighbouring beach cove for snorkelling — rent basic gear locally (~IDR 30,000–50,000).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and join a budget community yoga class if available nearby (~IDR 80,000–120,000). Enjoy a relaxed beachside evening watching local fishing boats return to shore.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit plate and Balinese black rice porridge (bubur injin) from a beachside warung (~IDR 30,000–45,000)
meals.lunch: Local wayang food stall — nasi campur (mixed rice with small portions of various dishes) (~IDR 35,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Grilled fresh fish at a beachfront warung — choose your fish by weight, very affordable (~IDR 60,000–90,000)

day_by_day.notes: Warm summer weather expected — apply sunscreen generously and stay hydrated. Water bottles can be refilled cheaply at most warungs.

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach walk at low tide to explore rock pools and natural sea life. Bring a journal or book and enjoy a slow Bali morning. Attempt a self-guided meditation session on a quiet stretch of beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a shared bemo (local minibus) or cheap scooter ride to a well-known surf beach nearby. Watch experienced surfers or take a budget beginner surf lesson (~IDR 150,000–200,000 including board rental — many schools offer group lessons). Bali's warm 25°C water makes it ideal for first-timers.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local night market (pasar malam) for street food browsing and people-watching. Pick up handmade souvenirs at very low prices — batik scarves, wooden carvings, and incense.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancakes — a Bali backpacker staple available at almost every warung (~IDR 20,000–35,000)
meals.lunch: Street food at the beach — sate lilit (Balinese minced fish satay) and corn on the cob (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Night market exploration — babi guling (suckling pig) if available, or mie goreng with egg (~IDR 30,000–50,000)

day_by_day.notes: 30mm average rain this month — carry a light rain poncho. Afternoon showers are brief and warm. Surf lessons are best in the morning when waves are more consistent.

day_by_day.morning: Attend an early morning yoga class at a budget yoga shala or community centre near the resort. Many offer drop-in rates (~IDR 80,000–150,000). Focus on a Vinyasa or Hatha flow to energise the day. Alternatively, follow a free YouTube yoga session on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Hindu temple — most coastal Bali villages have a beautiful pura (temple) free or with a small donation. Dress respectfully (sarong required — often loaned at the entrance). Explore the temple grounds and observe local offerings and ceremonies.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort. Try a budget traditional Balinese massage from a local therapist — many offer beachside sessions (~IDR 80,000–120,000 for 60 min). Watch the stars from the beach — minimal light pollution near the shore.

meals.breakfast: Nasi jinggo — small banana-leaf parcels of rice with tempe and chilli, sold by street vendors (~IDR 5,000–10,000 each, get 2–3)
meals.lunch: Warung lunch special — usually includes rice, vegetables, tofu/tempe, and a small protein (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Cook your own simple meal if the resort has a shared kitchen, using fresh market ingredients, or eat at a budget Indonesian restaurant (~IDR 40,000–60,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga classes in advance if possible during peak July season. Sarongs can be purchased at markets for ~IDR 30,000–50,000 and are useful throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach morning — swim, snorkel, or simply sunbathe. Explore tide pools at low tide. Hire a local fisherman for a short traditional boat ride along the coast (~IDR 50,000–100,000 negotiable) for a unique perspective of the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cheap shared ride or scooter to a famous viewpoint or cliff walk in the region. Enjoy panoramic ocean views — these are free and offer incredible photo opportunities. Walk along clifftop paths at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or donation-based Kecak fire dance performance if available in a nearby village or temple. This traditional Balinese dance is a cultural highlight and deeply memorable.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh juice from a budget café (~IDR 35,000–55,000)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a warung — ask them to wrap it in banana leaf for an authentic touch (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Beachfront BBQ warung — grilled prawns, fish, and vegetables with steamed rice (~IDR 70,000–100,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kecak dance performances are often held at sunset at clifftop temples — check local listings or ask resort staff. Entry is usually IDR 50,000–100,000.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga — either self-practice or join a local group session on the sand. The warm July mornings are perfect for outdoor practice. Focus on sun salutations facing the rising sun over the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip by scooter or cheap shared transport to a famous rice terrace area (e.g., Jatiluwih or Tegalalang if within range). Walk the terraces freely or for a small maintenance fee (~IDR 15,000–30,000). The lush green landscape contrasts beautifully with the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast. Visit a local village night market for dinner and cultural immersion. Pick up cheap local snacks like klepon (green rice balls with palm sugar) and pisang goreng (fried banana).

meals.breakfast: Traditional Balinese breakfast at the resort or nearby warung — jaja bali (rice cakes) and sweet black tea (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the rice terraces — buy provisions from a roadside stall (fruit, boiled eggs, tempe chips) (~IDR 20,000–35,000)
meals.dinner: Village warung near the market — nasi goreng special with fried egg and prawn crackers (~IDR 35,000–55,000)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is the most cost-effective way to explore inland Bali. Always wear a helmet and carry your international driving permit. Fuel is cheap (~IDR 10,000 per litre).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in, stretch on the balcony, or do a gentle yoga nidra session. Write in a travel journal or read on the beach. Midweek rest days help sustain energy for the full 13-day trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore local artisan workshops or batik-making demonstrations in the nearest village — often free to observe and very affordable to participate in (~IDR 50,000–80,000). Purchase a hand-dyed batik fabric as a meaningful souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset swim at the beach followed by a relaxed dinner. This is a great evening to try a slightly more indulgent budget meal — a full seafood platter at a mid-range warung is still very affordable in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Lazy brunch — avocado toast or eggs benedict at a budget café (~IDR 45,000–70,000)
meals.lunch: Skip or light snack — fresh coconut and tropical fruit from a beach vendor (~IDR 15,000–25,000)
meals.dinner: Seafood platter for one — lobster, prawns, fish, and squid grilled to order at a beachfront warung (~IDR 100,000–150,000 — a splurge but still budget-friendly)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for budget travellers who are also physically active with yoga and beach activities. Rehydrate well — coconut water is ideal and very cheap.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkelling or freediving at a nearby coral reef. Rent equipment locally (~IDR 50,000–80,000). Bali's warm waters host vibrant marine life including reef fish, sea turtles, and colourful corals. Best visibility is in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture garden if available in the area — some offer free or cheap tours (~IDR 30,000–50,000) and insight into Balinese sustainable agriculture. Learn about local herbs and spices used in traditional cooking.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a budget cooking class focused on Balinese cuisine (~IDR 150,000–250,000 including ingredients and a full meal). Learn to make satay, sambal, and lawar. This is one of the best value experiences in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-snorkel breakfast — toast with local jam and a boiled egg (~IDR 20,000–30,000)
meals.lunch: Post-snorkel warung meal — gado-gado (steamed vegetables with peanut sauce) (~IDR 30,000–45,000)
meals.dinner: Eat the meal you cooked in the cooking class — included in the class fee

day_by_day.notes: Confirm snorkelling spot safety with locals — some areas have strong currents. The cooking class meal counts as dinner so budget accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga — try a different style today such as Yin yoga or Restorative yoga at a local shala (~IDR 80,000–120,000). These slower practices complement the more active beach days. Ask the resort for recommendations on nearby studios.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon — build sandcastles, play beach volleyball with other travellers, or simply float in the warm sea. Explore a different section of the beach by walking 1–2 km in either direction from the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free beach bonfire if organised by locals or other travellers. Play guitar, share stories, and enjoy the simple pleasures of Bali's social beach culture. Many budget guesthouses and hostels organise these informally.

meals.breakfast: Açai bowl or granola with local yoghurt at a health-focused budget café (~IDR 40,000–65,000)
meals.lunch: Beachside food cart — corn on the cob, fried tofu skewers, and cold drinks (~IDR 20,000–35,000)
meals.dinner: Warung dinner — soto ayam (Indonesian chicken soup) with steamed rice and iced tea (~IDR 35,000–55,000)

day_by_day.notes: Yin yoga is excellent for stretching after days of swimming and surfing. If budget yoga studios are full, many free classes are posted on local community boards or Facebook groups.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike to a nearby hill or coastal headland for panoramic views — completely free and one of Bali's most rewarding experiences. Bring water and a light snack. The 25°C morning temperature makes hiking comfortable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a swim and rest. Spend the afternoon reading, journalling, or practising meditation on the beach. Consider a self-guided pranayama (breathing) session — free and deeply restorative.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a nearby village for a cultural evening walk. Observe temple preparations, local ceremonies, or simply watch daily life unfold. Stop at a roadside stall for a fresh young coconut as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy breakfast — nasi kuning (yellow rice cone) with boiled egg and tempe (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.lunch: Post-hike refreshment — fresh fruit salad and a cold jamu (traditional herbal drink) (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Village warung — bebek goreng (fried duck) with sambal and rice, a Balinese classic (~IDR 50,000–80,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check sunrise time for July in Bali (~06:15). Start the hike by 05:30 for the best experience. Bring a torch/headlamp and wear sturdy sandals or shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day beach yoga retreat — either self-curated or join a budget group beach yoga session. Spend 2 hours doing a complete practice: warm-up, asana flow, pranayama, and savasana on the sand with the sound of waves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby waterfall if accessible by scooter or cheap transport. Many of Bali's hidden waterfalls have small entry fees (~IDR 20,000–30,000) and offer a refreshing natural swim. The lush July greenery makes this especially beautiful.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style beach dinner with fellow travellers met during the trip. Organise a shared warung meal — group dining at a local restaurant is very affordable and social.

meals.breakfast: Healthy smoothie and wholegrain toast at a budget health café (~IDR 40,000–60,000)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the waterfall — buy provisions from a village stall near the entrance (~IDR 20,000–35,000)
meals.dinner: Shared group warung dinner — mixed dishes served family-style, split the bill (~IDR 60,000–90,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Waterfall swimming is refreshing but check water safety locally. Wear water shoes if the rocks are slippery. Group dining is a great way to try more dishes at lower individual cost.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — swim, snorkel, or simply sit and absorb the beauty of Bali's coastline. Take photos, collect memories, and do a slow mindful walk along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a local market — budget gifts include handmade bracelets (~IDR 10,000–20,000), incense sets (~IDR 15,000–25,000), and small wooden Ganesh statues (~IDR 20,000–50,000). Bargaining is expected and part of the fun.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset yoga session on the beach — a meaningful way to close the trip. Reflect on the journey, set intentions for home, and enjoy one last Bali sunset. Have a celebratory dinner at your favourite warung discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full Balinese breakfast spread — nasi goreng, fresh fruit, Balinese coffee, and jaja rice cakes (~IDR 45,000–65,000)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach café — club sandwich or Indonesian wrap (~IDR 40,000–60,000)
meals.dinner: Celebratory final dinner — return to your favourite warung or try a slightly upgraded local restaurant. Babi guling or full seafood platter (~IDR 100,000–150,000)

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags tonight to ease the morning departure. Keep one change of clothes accessible for travel day. Double-check flight details and arrange airport transport in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the beach — wake early for one last Bali sunrise. Do a short 20-minute yoga or stretching session to prepare your body for travel. Take a final dip in the ocean if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Head to the airport via pre-arranged Grab or shared shuttle. Allow extra time for Bali traffic — aim to arrive at the airport 2.5–3 hours before departure. Browse duty-free for any last-minute affordable Bali coffee or chocolate gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ngurah Rai International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, yoga, culture, and budget-friendly Bali living.

meals.breakfast: Final warung breakfast — banana pancakes, fresh juice, and Balinese coffee (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.lunch: Airport food court — nasi goreng or bakso soup (~IDR 50,000–80,000 — slightly pricier at airport)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: A well-managed 13-day Bali budget trip can be achieved for approximately $30–$50 USD per day including accommodation, food, transport, and activities. Keep receipts and track spending to stay on target. Bali's warmth — both in weather and people — makes it one of the world's best budget destinations.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali (flight LH lands at 13:00) — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Ngurah Rai International Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort (~45–60 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely first stroll along the beachfront to get oriented. Dip your toes in the Indian Ocean and enjoy the warm 25°C weather from the resort beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beach near the resort. Explore the immediate surroundings and enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's beachside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport — try a local warung (Indonesian food stall) inside the terminal for nasi goreng (~IDR 45,000)
meals.dinner: Resort beachside restaurant — grilled seafood platter with steamed rice and local sambal (~IDR 180,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Hydrate well and use sunscreen. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM for Indonesian Rupiah.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a sunrise beach yoga session on the resort's private beach (many Bali resorts offer complimentary or low-cost morning yoga at 7:00–8:30 AM). Follow with a swim in the calm morning sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local beach market or the closest beach village to pick up fresh tropical fruits and handmade souvenirs. Spend time snorkeling or paddleboarding at the resort beach (equipment rental ~IDR 100,000/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby beach bar or café for Bali's famous Kecak fire dance performance if available locally, or watch the sunset with a fresh coconut in hand. Dinner at a local warung near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a nearby café — fresh fruit, eggs, and Balinese black rice porridge (bubur injin) (~IDR 80,000)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beachside warung — grilled fish with plecing kangkung (water spinach) and rice (~IDR 90,000)
meals.dinner: Local warung dinner — mie goreng (fried noodles) or babi guling (suckling pig) with local beer (~IDR 120,000)

day_by_day.notes: July is dry season in Bali with only ~30mm rain — ideal beach weather. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga class at a dedicated yoga studio near the resort (Bali has world-class yoga centers; drop-in classes typically IDR 150,000–200,000). Many studios offer ocean-view or jungle-view settings for an immersive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby Hindu temple — visit a coastal sea temple (pura segara) accessible from the resort area. Learn about Balinese Hindu culture and watch daily offerings being placed.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through a local night market (pasar malam) for street food and local crafts. Enjoy a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa (~IDR 120,000 for 60 min).

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl and avocado toast at a trendy beachside café (~IDR 85,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near the temple — nasi campur (mixed rice with various sides) (~IDR 60,000)
meals.dinner: Night market street food — satay skewers, pisang goreng (fried banana), and fresh juice (~IDR 80,000)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples — bring a sarong and sash (often available to borrow at temple entrances). Balinese temples are active places of worship; be respectful.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Uluwatu Temple — one of Bali's most iconic clifftop sea temples perched 70m above the Indian Ocean. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Explore the surrounding cliffs and watch surfers at Uluwatu Beach below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Padang Padang Beach or Bingin Beach (near Uluwatu) — two of Bali's most beautiful and secluded beaches. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the dramatic limestone cliffs. Rent a sun lounger (~IDR 50,000).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Uluwatu for the famous Kecak Fire Dance performance at sunset (starts ~18:00, tickets ~IDR 100,000). The clifftop setting with the ocean backdrop is unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or grab a quick local breakfast — jaja bali (Balinese rice cakes) and Bali coffee (~IDR 50,000)
meals.lunch: Beach café at Padang Padang — fresh grilled fish tacos or seafood noodles (~IDR 110,000)
meals.dinner: Clifftop restaurant near Uluwatu — wood-fired pizza or Indonesian fusion with ocean views (~IDR 200,000)

day_by_day.notes: Watch out for monkeys at Uluwatu Temple — they are notorious for snatching sunglasses, hats, and phones. Hire a private driver for the day (~IDR 400,000–500,000) for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Morning surf lesson at a local surf school near the resort (Bali is world-renowned for surfing; beginner lessons ~IDR 300,000 including board and instructor for 2 hours). Kuta, Seminyak, or Canggu beaches are ideal for beginners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and recover at the resort pool or beach. Explore the resort's spa for a traditional Balinese boreh body scrub treatment (~IDR 250,000).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Seminyak or Kuta area for shopping and nightlife — browse boutique shops along Jalan Laksmana (Eat Street). Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Healthy bowl at a surf café — acai bowl, granola, and fresh coconut water (~IDR 95,000)
meals.lunch: Post-surf warung near the beach — nasi goreng with fried egg and prawn crackers (~IDR 70,000)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Seminyak — wood-fired seafood or Balinese duck (bebek betutu) with rice wine (~IDR 220,000)

day_by_day.notes: Beginner surfers should stick to mellow beach breaks. Always surf with an instructor on Day 1 of surfing. Stay hydrated — the Bali sun is strong even in warm summer conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — Bali's cultural and spiritual heart (~1–1.5 hours from the coast). Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (IDR 80,000 entry) and walk through the ancient temples within.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's Tegallalang Rice Terraces — iconic UNESCO-listed green terraces with dramatic views. Walk the pathways between the paddies (~IDR 50,000 donation). Visit local artisan workshops nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Ubud night — watch a traditional Legong dance performance at Ubud Palace (IDR 100,000). Browse Ubud Art Market for batik textiles, wood carvings, and silver jewelry.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Ubud warung — traditional Balinese rijsttafel (rice table) with multiple small dishes (~IDR 130,000)
meals.dinner: Ubud restaurant with rice terrace view — organic Balinese cuisine and fresh turmeric latte (~IDR 180,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a driver for the Ubud day trip (~IDR 450,000 return). Ubud is cooler than the coast — bring a light layer. Bargaining is expected at the art market; start at 50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga and meditation session at the resort or a beachfront yoga platform. Focus on a restorative practice after several busy days. Follow with a slow beach walk collecting shells.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) session at a nearby calm bay or beach. Many coastal areas near Bali resorts offer excellent snorkeling with vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach bonfire or beach cinema event (check resort activities board). Enjoy a quiet evening with a good book and the sound of the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — fresh tropical fruit platter, Balinese pancakes (dadar gulung), and Bali coffee (~IDR 100,000)
meals.lunch: Light beach picnic — pick up fresh fruit, bread, and local snacks from a nearby minimarket (~IDR 60,000)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — BBQ night or local set menu with live acoustic music (~IDR 200,000)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally a rest and recharge day — a balanced itinerary includes downtime. Listen to your body and enjoy the natural beauty around you.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most photographed sea temples built on a rocky outcrop in the ocean. Best visited at low tide when you can walk across to the base. Arrive by 9:00 AM (~IDR 60,000 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Tanah Lot area — visit Pura Batu Bolong nearby and walk along the dramatic coastline. Stop at local craft stalls for handmade silver jewelry and textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Book a traditional Balinese four-hand massage at a reputable spa (~IDR 350,000 for 90 min). Dinner at a romantic beachside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Café near resort — eggs benedict with smoked salmon and fresh juice (~IDR 110,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near Tanah Lot — fresh coconut, grilled corn, and nasi campur (~IDR 75,000)
meals.dinner: Romantic beachfront restaurant — candlelit dinner with grilled lobster or snapper (~IDR 280,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is very crowded at sunset — visit in the morning for a more peaceful experience. The temple itself is sacred and non-Hindus cannot enter the inner sanctum.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga flow class at a beachside yoga shala (open-air yoga pavilion). Focus on sun salutations facing the ocean at sunrise. Many studios in Bali offer this magical experience (~IDR 150,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Balinese cooking class (~2–3 hours, ~IDR 350,000) — learn to make traditional dishes like satay, tempeh manis, and black rice pudding. Usually includes a market visit to buy fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Apply your new cooking skills — recreate a dish at the resort's communal kitchen if available, or enjoy dinner at a local restaurant featuring the dishes you learned to cook.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast — banana, dates, and Bali coffee (~IDR 40,000)
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you cooked in the cooking class (usually included in the class fee)
meals.dinner: Mid-range Balinese restaurant — bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck) with steamed rice and lawar salad (~IDR 170,000)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes are a fantastic cultural experience and a great souvenir skill. Book in advance as popular classes fill up quickly. The market visit at dawn is a highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Water sports morning — try parasailing, jet skiing, or banana boat rides at a nearby water sports beach (~IDR 200,000–400,000 per activity). Tanjung Benoa is Bali's water sports hub if accessible from your resort area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Balinese healer (balian) for a traditional blessing ceremony or energy healing session — a deeply authentic cultural experience unique to Bali (~IDR 200,000–300,000 donation).
day_by_day.evening: Chill evening at the resort — enjoy the pool at golden hour, sip on a Bali Sling cocktail, and watch the stars emerge over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Balinese black rice porridge with coconut milk and palm sugar (~IDR 80,000)
meals.lunch: Beachside café near the water sports area — fish and chips or prawn tempura with cold Bintang beer (~IDR 130,000)
meals.dinner: Resort pool bar — tapas-style sharing plates and tropical cocktails (~IDR 220,000)

day_by_day.notes: Always use licensed and reputable water sports operators with proper safety equipment. For the balian visit, go with a local guide or trusted recommendation to ensure authenticity.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mount Batur — Bali's active volcano with a stunning crater lake. Depart very early (~2:00 AM) for a pre-dawn hike to the summit to watch sunrise from 1,717m elevation (guided trek ~IDR 400,000–600,000 including guide and breakfast on the summit).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Soak tired legs in the pool or treat yourself to a hot stone massage (~IDR 300,000). Rest and nap.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle sunset beach walk. Low-key dinner at a nearby restaurant — let the volcano adventure sink in.

meals.breakfast: Bananas and energy bars before the hike; hard-boiled eggs and toast cooked on volcanic steam at the summit (included in guide fee)
meals.lunch: Post-hike warung near Mount Batur — hearty nasi goreng and fresh juice (~IDR 80,000)
meals.dinner: Cozy restaurant near resort — wood-fired pizza or pasta with a glass of Hatten Bali wine (~IDR 190,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Batur hike is moderately challenging but accessible for most fitness levels. Wear layers as the summit is cold before sunrise. Book a licensed guide through your hotel or a reputable agency.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to your favorite beach spot from the trip. Swim, snorkel, or simply float in the warm Indian Ocean. Reflect on the journey and soak in the Bali sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a local art market or boutique shop. Look for Balinese silver jewelry, hand-painted batik, carved wooden figures, and locally produced Luwak coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of the best restaurants in the area — splurge slightly on a special meal to celebrate the trip. Watch the final Bali sunset over the ocean with a cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Favorite café revisit — smoothie bowl, fresh tropical fruits, and Bali coffee (~IDR 90,000)
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh coconut, grilled corn, and satay sticks from a beach vendor (~IDR 60,000)
meals.dinner: Upscale beachfront restaurant — 3-course set menu with Balinese specialties and sunset views (~IDR 350,000)

day_by_day.notes: Pack tonight for departure tomorrow. Keep a small bag accessible for the journey. Tip your hotel staff and drivers generously — service workers in Bali rely heavily on tips.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga or meditation on the beach — a peaceful send-off from Bali. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Check out and arrange airport transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — if time allows, visit a final nearby attraction, enjoy a last coffee at a beachside café, or simply relax at the resort until transfer time.
day_by_day.evening: Airport transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Depart Bali with unforgettable memories.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go all out on the tropical spread (~IDR 100,000 or included)
meals.lunch: Airport or pre-airport café — light meal before the flight (~IDR 100,000)
meals.dinner: On the flight or at the destination airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer with the hotel the night before. Bali traffic can be unpredictable — allow extra time. Declare any food items (Luwak coffee, fresh fruits) at customs when returning home. Selamat jalan — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort, Bali. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your beachfront suite. Enjoy a welcome drink and resort orientation. Take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to acclimate to the warm Bali air.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, watching the golden hour over the Indian Ocean. Light exploration of the resort grounds, pool area, and spa facilities.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant. Enjoy a curated Indonesian tasting menu featuring grilled seafood, nasi goreng royale, and tropical desserts. Pair with a fine Riesling or fresh coconut cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Request a beachfront suite upgrade upon check-in if available. Ask the concierge to pre-book spa treatments and yoga sessions for the coming days. Hydrate well after the flight — Bali humidity can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the private beach or resort's open-air yoga pavilion. A certified instructor leads a 75-minute Hatha or Vinyasa flow as the sun rises over the ocean. Follow with a refreshing ocean dip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling excursion along Bali's pristine coastal reef. A resort-arranged boat takes you to a secluded snorkeling spot with vibrant coral and tropical fish. Return by mid-afternoon for a relaxing session at the infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside dinner under the stars at a premium seaside restaurant near the resort. Choose from freshly grilled lobster, Balinese spiced duck, or a seafood platter with local sambal sauces.

meals.breakfast: Lavish resort breakfast buffet featuring tropical fruits, Balinese jamu juice, eggs benedict, smoked salmon, and freshly baked pastries.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled prawn skewers, avocado salad, and fresh coconut water served by the infinity pool.
meals.dinner: Premium beachside restaurant near the resort — grilled whole lobster with garlic butter, Balinese black rice, and a chilled Sauvignon Blanc.

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Book the sunrise yoga session through the resort spa desk the evening before. Optimal snorkeling visibility is typically between 9:00–11:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Private Balinese sound healing and meditation session at the resort's wellness center. A traditional healer uses singing bowls, gongs, and sacred chants to promote deep relaxation. Duration: 90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural tour of Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rocky outcrop. Private guide explains the temple's Hindu-Balinese spiritual significance. Explore the surrounding cliffs and coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a traditional Balinese massage at the spa (60–90 minutes). Followed by a private dining experience on your suite's terrace or the beach with a curated set menu.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered to your terrace — fresh tropical fruit platter, Balinese porridge (bubur), freshly squeezed juices, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium warung near Tanah Lot — nasi campur (mixed rice plate), satay lilit, and fresh lemonade.
meals.dinner: Private terrace or beach dining at the resort — slow-roasted Balinese suckling pig (babi guling), steamed jasmine rice, and a bottle of Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is especially beautiful at sunset — time the visit for late afternoon if preferred. Wear a sarong at the temple (provided on-site). Book the sound healing session in advance at the resort wellness desk.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Yin Yoga and breathwork class at the resort pavilion overlooking the ocean. 90-minute session focusing on flexibility, stress relief, and mindfulness. Followed by a guided meditation walk along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private surfing lesson on a nearby beginner-friendly beach. An expert instructor provides one-on-one coaching. Even non-surfers will be standing on the board within the session. Equipment and rash guard included.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktail cruise along Bali's southern coastline on a private chartered catamaran. Watch the sunset from the water with canapés, champagne, and a live acoustic guitarist.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoothie bowls, acai, granola, poached eggs on sourdough, and cold-pressed juices.
meals.lunch: Beach shack lunch post-surfing — fresh grilled fish tacos, sweet potato fries, and iced hibiscus tea.
meals.dinner: Fine dining dinner aboard the catamaran or at a top-rated Bali restaurant — seared tuna tataki, wagyu beef tenderloin, and a premium dessert pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran sunset cruise at least 2 days in advance through the resort concierge. Surfing lessons are suitable for all levels — inform the instructor of your experience beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided yoga and Pranayama (breathwork) session at sunrise on the beach. 90 minutes of Ashtanga-style practice followed by a 20-minute guided breathing session. Ideal for deepening your yoga practice in an inspiring natural setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Seminyak area via private driver — visit luxury boutiques, art galleries, and design stores. Browse high-end Balinese crafts, hand-woven textiles, and artisan jewelry. Stop at a renowned local art gallery.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Seminyak's most acclaimed fine dining restaurants — a sophisticated setting with panoramic views, innovative cuisine blending French techniques with Indonesian ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast — banana, almond butter toast, and green tea. Full breakfast after yoga: eggs your way, avocado toast, tropical fruit, and freshly brewed Bali coffee.
meals.lunch: Trendy café lunch in Seminyak — grain bowls, cold-pressed juices, and raw desserts.
meals.dinner: Top-tier Seminyak restaurant — slow-cooked lamb shoulder with Balinese spices, truffle risotto, and a curated wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is approximately 20–40 minutes from most beachfront resorts depending on traffic. Arrange a private driver for the day for comfort and flexibility. Bargaining is acceptable in local markets but not in boutiques.

day_by_day.morning: Full luxury spa day begins with a traditional Balinese boreh body scrub and wrap (volcanic clay, turmeric, and ginger). Followed by a 90-minute hot stone massage and a floral bath ritual in a private outdoor soaking tub.
day_by_day.afternoon: Floating yoga session in the resort's infinity pool — a unique and playful experience using floating mats. Alternatively, enjoy a restorative yoga nidra session in the shaded garden pavilion.
day_by_day.evening: Private Balinese cooking class at the resort or a nearby premium culinary school. Learn to prepare 3–4 traditional dishes including satay, gado-gado, and black rice pudding. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Spa-day wellness breakfast — warm golden milk, chia pudding, fresh papaya, and herbal teas.
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch — quinoa salad, cold coconut soup, and fresh fruit skewers served in the spa garden.
meals.dinner: Your own Balinese cooking class creations — satay lilit, gado-gado, nasi goreng, and black rice pudding with palm sugar.

day_by_day.notes: The spa day is best enjoyed on a rest day between active excursions. Book the cooking class at least 2 days in advance. Most premium cooking classes include a market visit — confirm with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Uluwatu — one of Bali's most dramatic clifftop temples. Visit the iconic Pura Luhur Uluwatu perched 70 meters above the Indian Ocean. Explore the surrounding cliff paths and watch resident monkeys in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-temple beach time at Padang Padang or Bingin Beach — two of Bali's most beautiful and relatively secluded beaches near Uluwatu. Swim, sunbathe, or simply enjoy the dramatic limestone cliff scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu amphitheater at sunset — a mesmerizing traditional Balinese dance performed against the backdrop of the setting sun over the ocean. One of Bali's most iconic cultural experiences.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread of local and continental options.
meals.lunch: Cliffside lunch at a premium Uluwatu restaurant — fresh grilled fish, Balinese salads, and tropical smoothies with panoramic ocean views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated Jimbaran Bay seafood restaurant — fresh catch grilled over coconut husks, served on the beach with candles and live gamelan music.

day_by_day.notes: Wear a sarong at Uluwatu Temple (provided on-site). Keep belongings secure around the monkeys — they are known to snatch sunglasses and bags. Book Kecak performance tickets in advance (approx. 6:00 PM start). Jimbaran Bay is a short drive from Uluwatu.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga session — a 75-minute Vinyasa flow on the private beach as the sun rises. Focus on sun salutations, warrior sequences, and heart-opening poses. Followed by a guided journaling session in the beach garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided snorkeling or scuba diving experience at a premium dive site near the resort. Explore Bali's underwater world with colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral gardens. All equipment provided.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic beachfront dinner for two (or solo luxury dining) — a private table set on the sand with lanterns, flowers, and a personalized menu curated by the resort's head chef.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga nourishing breakfast — smoothie bowls, protein-rich eggs, Balinese granola, and fresh tropical juices.
meals.lunch: Beachside light lunch — grilled calamari, Caesar salad, and sparkling water with citrus.
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dining — five-course tasting menu: amuse-bouche, lobster bisque, sea bass ceviche, wagyu beef medallion, and a chocolate lava cake with vanilla bean ice cream. Champagne pairing available.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private beachfront dinner through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance for the best setup and personalization. Scuba diving requires a PADI certification for deeper dives — snorkeling is available for all.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — Bali's cultural heartland. Begin with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary, a lush jungle reserve home to hundreds of Balinese long-tailed macaques and ancient Hindu temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's vibrant art scene — visit the Neka Art Museum or Agung Rai Museum of Art (ARMA), showcasing traditional and contemporary Balinese paintings. Browse the Ubud Art Market for premium crafts and handmade goods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Legong or Barong dance performance at one of Ubud's royal palace venues. Dinner at one of Ubud's celebrated farm-to-table restaurants with rice terrace views.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with Balinese coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a renowned Ubud restaurant — organic salads, tempeh curry, and fresh coconut water amidst jungle greenery.
meals.dinner: Premium Ubud farm-to-table restaurant — slow-roasted duck with Balinese spices, organic vegetables, and a curated natural wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1–1.5 hours from beachfront areas — depart by 8:30 AM for a full day. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Monkey Forest. Keep valuables in a zipped bag around the monkeys. Book the dance performance in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury wellness morning — begin with a 60-minute Kundalini yoga session at the resort, followed by a private Ayurvedic consultation and personalized wellness treatment at the spa (abhyanga oil massage or shirodhara head treatment).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private catamaran or speedboat trip to Nusa Lembongan island — a pristine island just off Bali's southeast coast. Explore crystal-clear waters, visit Devil's Tear cliff viewpoint, and relax on secluded white sand beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by sunset. Enjoy a quiet evening with a private in-suite dinner or a relaxed meal at the resort's al fresco restaurant with ocean views and live ambient music.

meals.breakfast: Wellness breakfast — warm lemon water, overnight oats, fresh berries, and herbal detox tea.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on Nusa Lembongan — grilled fish, coconut rice, and fresh lime juice at a beachside café.
meals.dinner: Resort al fresco dinner — pan-seared barramundi, roasted vegetables, saffron risotto, and a glass of chilled Chardonnay.

day_by_day.notes: Nusa Lembongan boat transfers take approximately 30 minutes from Sanur or Benoa Harbor. Arrange transport through the resort concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up for the island visit.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise beach meditation and yoga nidra session (yoga sleep) — a deeply restorative 90-minute guided practice on the sand. Ideal for mental reset and deep relaxation. Followed by a mindful beach walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Berawa or Canggu area via private driver — visit trendy beach clubs, boutique wellness studios, and artisan coffee shops. Enjoy a session at one of Canggu's premium beach clubs with pool access and cabana service.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at a rooftop bar in Canggu with panoramic views of the rice fields and ocean. Dinner at a celebrated Canggu restaurant known for its creative modern Asian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast — tropical fruit platter, Balinese eggs benedict, fresh juices, and Bali single-origin coffee.
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — gourmet burgers, truffle fries, and fresh açaí bowls by the pool.
meals.dinner: Canggu fine dining — tasting menu with Japanese-Balinese fusion: miso black cod, wagyu gyoza, and yuzu panna cotta.

day_by_day.notes: Canggu beach clubs can be busy on weekends — reserve a cabana or daybed in advance. The drive from beachfront resorts to Canggu is approximately 20–40 minutes depending on traffic.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day beach morning — a leisurely sunrise walk along the private beach, followed by a gentle yoga stretch session on the sand. Spend time swimming in the warm Indian Ocean and relaxing in a hammock under palm trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping — visit a curated selection of premium Bali boutiques for high-end souvenirs: hand-crafted silver jewelry, premium batik fabrics, artisan ceramics, and Balinese wood carvings. A private shopper can be arranged.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luxury dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — a special chef's table experience or a private beachside dinner with a personalized multi-course menu celebrating your Bali journey.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread including made-to-order omelets, smoked salmon, tropical fruits, and freshly baked croissants.
meals.lunch: Poolside farewell lunch — lobster rolls, truffle pasta, and sparkling rosé.
meals.dinner: Chef's table farewell dinner — eight-course degustation menu with wine pairing: Balinese-inspired dishes showcasing the finest local ingredients, from spiced tuna tartare to coconut panna cotta with passion fruit coulis.

day_by_day.notes: Request the chef's table experience at least 3 days in advance — it is often fully booked. Pack souvenirs carefully — Balinese ceramics and wood carvings may need bubble wrap. Confirm checkout time and airport transfer for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga session on the beach — a gentle, reflective 60-minute practice to close your Bali journey. Followed by a relaxing soak in the outdoor bathtub or a final dip in the infinity pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely checkout after a final resort breakfast. Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Arrive with ample time before departure. Enjoy the resort's late checkout option if available (usually until 2:00 PM with prior arrangement).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry the warmth, calm, and memories of 13 extraordinary days on this magical island.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — your favorite dishes from the trip. Treat yourself to a special order of Balinese pancakes with palm sugar syrup, tropical fruits, and a last cup of Bali kopi.
meals.lunch: Light airport lounge lunch or a final café stop near the resort before transfer.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at your connecting airport.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer the night before through the concierge. Bali airport (Ngurah Rai) recommends arriving 3 hours before international flights. Check baggage allowance for any premium souvenirs or spa products purchased during the trip. Consider a premium airport lounge for a comfortable pre-departure experience.
